title: A trigger word is not a directive
statement: A check triggered by a word list fires on ordinary uses of its words, so make it require an explicit phrase and filter out narrative and negated uses.
example: Ordering items containing the word 'model' or 'figure' were forced to a stimulus score of 0.0.
detail: A stimulus mismatch check injected an instruction to score the stimulus 0.0 into ordering items that contained words like 'model' or 'figure', overriding correct scores (commit 20bb29e in `icloud-work/inceptbench`). The visual-reference pattern now leaves out bare 'figure', which collided with 'figure-eight' in an item about a bee dance (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/evaluators/question.py`), and a filter drops narrative uses such as 'a family is looking at a map', which describe a scenario rather than tell the student to consult a picture (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/tools/stimulus_reference_detector.py`). Checks that read the judge's own reasoning were narrowed the same way: broad cues like 'causal' fired on correct explanations, so the guard needs an explicit admission phrase and drops negated forms such as 'not misleading' (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/evaluators/guards.py`).
against: A later run found: For misconception screens a Grade 5 reading course chose the opposite: its gate fails a literal misconception phrase even inside a negation, rejected alternative or correction, by its own account deliberately stricter than a contextual judgment. A Grade 3 gate went this record's way and added a negation guard; which scope is right is an open question (`incept-package-hub/course-packages/courses/g5-reading/review/evidence/science-process.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/courses/g5-reading/review/evidence/science-process.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g5-reading-v2/docs/SCIENCE_MISCONCEPTION_CHECK.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`incept-package-hub/course-packages/courses/g5-reading/review/evidence/science-process.md`).

evidence.quote: Sequence questions have no visual stimuli — the mismatch check injected "MUST score stimulus_quality = 0.0" for items containing words like "model" or "figure", overriding correct sequence scores.
Bare "figure" / "figures" are intentionally excluded because they # collide with content phrases like "figure-eight" (#371 bee dance).

Narrative/descriptive "is looking at" is NOT a directive to the student. # Phrases like "A family is looking at a map" describe a scenario; they do # not instruct the student to consult a visual artifact.

Admission keywords are kept narrow on purpose: broader cues like "causal" or "mechanism" trigger far too often on factually-correct explanations that merely mention causation, so the guard requires an explicit admission phrase. Negated forms ("not misleading", "isn't a factual error") are filtered out via a negation-prefix post-check.
